title: Signal Atlas: sessionization and rollback checklist
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a compact, operational-first guide for building a small "Signal Atlas" — a curated set of signals (metrics + trace anchors + widgets) that makes session-level problems visible and provides explicit rollback/mitigation anchors for oncall teams.

Why Signal Atlas?
- We have too many panel-level metrics and not enough session-centric lenses. When users (or internal tenants) see weird behavior, SREs and product engineers need a compact path from symptom -> trace -> rollback.
- Goal: make a 6–10 signal slice per major surface (hosted API, dedicated pools, private) that is fast to query and actionable.

Design principles (short):
- Session-first: prefer signals that can be correlated to a session or request id.
- Anchor to traces: for each metric include a trace-anchor (span id mapping or sample key).
- Rollback-friendly: each signal should map to at least one mitigation action with measurable effect within 5 minutes.
- Cost bounded: sampling and panel cardinality constrained to keep query budget predictable.

Atlas structure (recommended):
1) Session existence & health signals (3)
   - session.count (per minute, by route, by region) — count of unique session_id seen in last minute (derive from request headers).
   - session.latency.p50/p95 (end-to-end request time from ingress to last token emitted) — tag by model_family, route.
   - session.error_rate (per-minute ratio of 4xx/5xx spikes and internal validation errors).
   Trace anchor: sample 1/200 sessions for full-trace capture; attach request_id tag to trace.
   Rollback anchor: if session.count drops >=50% + latency up 2x, switch routing policy to fallback model-variant A.

2) KV/prefix cache warmth signals (2)
   - kvcache.hit_rate (per-tenant, per-pool) — 1m window, rolling median and tail.
   - kvcache.tail-latency (99th percentile lookup latency) — indicates inefficient cache paths or cold storage fallback.
   Trace anchor: instrument span "kv.lookup" with cache.hit boolean.
   Rollback anchor: on warm-rate collapse, increase burst-capacity for dedicated pools or enable cached-prefix fallback.

3) Token generation & throughput signals (2)
   - tokens.per-second (per-pool) — helps detect throttling/backpressure.
   - decode.latency.p99 (per-model, per-seq-len-bucket) — long tails often indicate kernel fallback or quantization mismatch.
   Trace anchor: capture last-token spans and GPU-scheduler trace id.
   Rollback anchor: if tokens/sec drops and decode.p99 spikes, reduce batch size / fall back to lower-precision variant.

Signal definitions (quick reference):
- session.count: distinct(session_id) over interval. Important to dedupe identical session ids produced by retries.
- session.latency: measured in ms; start = ingress.request_received, end = response.last_token_sent. 
- session.error_rate: count(errors)/count(requests); error categories: retriable, nonretriable, model-hallucination-flag.
- kvcache.hit_rate: hits / (hits + misses) from kv.lookup span.
- decode.latency: span decode.iteration or gpu.exec wall time aggregated per-request.

Sampling & trace capture policy (must protect query budget):
- Default sampling: 1 in 200 sessions for full trace.
- Progressive increase on anomaly: if session.error_rate for a route > 1.5x baseline for 3 minutes, escalate sampling to 1 in 20 for that route for 20 minutes.
- High-value tenant sampling: for customers on Dedicated/Private tagged as enterprise, sampling baseline is 1 in 50.
- Redaction: traces must strip prompt content for PII-sensitive tenants; use token hashing for correlation ids.

Dashboard layout (wireframe notes):
- Top row: high-level session health (session.count trend, session.latency p95, error_rate). Minimal color palette and single-number sparklines.
- Middle row: cache signals + token throughput (kv.hit_rate, kv.tail-latency, tokens/sec).
- Bottom row: incident anchors (heatmap of routes by error spike, list of sampled trace ids with quick links).
- Small panel: current sampling multiplier and active mitigations/rollouts.

Alerting and runbook linkage (practical):
- Alert 1: session_count_drop (threshold: drop >40% vs trailing-1h baseline AND p95 latency increase >1.8x). Severity: P1. Owner: oncall-sre. Playbook: check pool capacity, check recent rollout, flip routing to variant B (fast; configured in runtime toggle).
- Alert 2: kvcache_warmth_degradation (hit_rate <70% for 10m). Severity: P2. Playbook: check prefix eviction logs, rehydrate cache for top-10 tenants, enable prefix-fallback mode.
- Alert 3: decode_tail_surge (decode.p99 > configured threshold for model_family). Severity: P1 if tokens/sec concurrently drops. Playbook: check kernel fallback logs and abort heavy rollouts.

Rollback checklist (decision tree snippets):
- On seeing session health failure: 1) Confirm via sampled traces that root cause is model variant / kernel fallback / cold cache. 2) If model variant: rollback to previous stable model (use canary window flags). 3) If kernel fallback: re-route to hardware pool with compatible kernel. 4) If cold cache: trigger cache rewarm script and enable short-term prefix-caching.

Ownership & decay rules:
- Each signal must have an "owner" (team + primary eng). Owner responsibilities: define alert thresholds, own sampling budget, instrument trace anchors, maintain dashboard widget.
- Signal TTL: if a signal is unused in runbooks or not surfaced in oncall flows for 90d, place in "staging" then archive after 180d.

Quick queries and hints (SQL / metrics language pseudo):
- session.count: SELECT count_distinct(session_id) FROM requests WHERE route = 'api.chat' AND ts > now() - interval '1 minute' GROUP BY region;
- kv.hit_rate: SELECT sum(hit)/sum(hit+miss) FROM kv_lookup WHERE pool = 'dedicated-nv' AND ts > now() - interval '5 minutes';
- decode.p99: SELECT quantile(0.99)(duration_ms) FROM spans WHERE span_name = 'decode.iter' AND model_family = 'redwood-v1' AND ts > now() - interval '10 minutes';

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- What is an acceptable oncall sampling cap (queries/min) for paid tenants vs internal staging clusters? Need SRE & analytics input.
- Should we bake the sampling-multiplier into alert payloads so PagerDuty shows when we escalated sampling? (Pros: faster triage; Cons: more noisy).
- Validate that trace redaction function meets legal for EU-regulated customers. Priya to confirm with security.
- Run a small pilot: build atlas for 2 routes (chat-stream, embeddings) and measure operator time-to-resolution vs current baseline.

Appendix: one-page operator cheat-sheet (cut/paste into runbook)
- "Session drop + latency up" -> Check recent model rollouts (console/commit log). If rollout in last 30m -> rollback. If no rollout -> sample traces for route (escalate sampling) -> look for kernel-fallback spans -> if present, switch pools.
- "KV warm-rate low" -> Check eviction rate and recent cache config changes -> rehydrate top prefixes -> enable temporary prefix-fallback.
- "Decode tail high" -> Reduce batch size and pin older model variant until fix.

End notes: lightweight, operational first. Not a complete instrument taxonomy; meant as a focused, fast-to-iterate atlas for 2–3 oncall shifts to test. Feedback cycle: capture notes in confluence:OBS-SIGNAL-ATLAS-42 and iterate weekly.

-- Aisha (draft).
